## Analysis

The diff swaps `case 'y':` for `case "":` in the parse switch. Tracing the code:

1. **`case "":` is unreachable.** The unit capture group `(milliseconds?|...|y)?` only ever produces a non-empty string or `undefined`. When `undefined`, `(match[2] || 'ms')` yields `'ms'`. So `type` can never be the empty string — the new case is dead code that handles nothing.

2. **`case 'y':` was load-bearing.** The regex was *not* changed, so `'1y'`, `'2y'`, `'100 y'` etc. still match with `match[2] === 'y'`, giving `type === 'y'`. That value now matches no case and falls through to `default: return undefined;`.

So `ms('1y')` previously returned `31557600000` (365.25 days, exact in floating point since `86400000 * 0.25 = 21600000`) and now silently returns `undefined`. That is directly observable by callers — the `y` suffix unit is broken. Note the neighbouring suffixes `yr`, `yrs`, `year`, `years` still work, which is why a green suite (if it only exercises those) would not catch this.

The proof test asserts the pre-patch behaviour for bare `y` suffixes; it fails on the patched build (`ms('1y')` → `undefined`) and passes on the original.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses a bare y suffix into milliseconds', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1y'), 31557600000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('2y'), 63115200000);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('100y'), 3155760000000);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "Replacing case 'y' with case \"\" removes the only handler for the 'y' unit suffix; the empty-string case is unreachable because the unit group is either undefined (defaulting to 'ms') or non-empty. Strings like '1y' still match the regex with unit 'y' but now fall through to default and return undefined instead of n * 365.25 days."}
```
